config.title: WebSocket Hook

intro.title: WebSocket Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom Vue composable (hook) to manage a WebSocket connection. You will learn how to use Vue's reactive state and lifecycle hooks to create a reusable function that connects to a WebSocket server, listens for messages, and sends data. The main technologies involved are the WebSocket API for real-time communication and Vue's ref and onMounted/onUnmounted functions. By the end, you'll have a practical hook that can be integrated into any Vue component to handle live data streams.
intro.usecase: WebSocket hooks are essential for building real-time features in modern web applications. You'll use them in live chat interfaces like Slack or Discord, where messages appear instantly without page refreshes. They're also critical for financial dashboards that display live stock prices, collaborative editing tools like Google Docs showing simultaneous changes, and multiplayer game interfaces updating player positions in real-time. As a Vue developer, creating custom WebSocket hooks lets you encapsulate connection logic and state management for these dynamic user experiences.

objectives: Implement a custom WebSocket hook using Vue's Composition API
Initialize WebSocket connections with configurable URL parameters
Bind WebSocket event listeners to reactive state updates
Control WebSocket message transmission through custom methods
Integrate the WebSocket hook into a Vue component for real-time data display
Manipulate component state based on WebSocket connection status
Configure automatic cleanup of WebSocket connections on component unmount

steps.title: Import Vue and the required composition API functions
steps.instruction: Import ref, onMounted, onUnmounted, and reactive from 'vue'.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement to bring in all four functions from the Vue package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple functions from a module
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import the required Vue composition API functions here
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have the necessary imports for creating reactive state and lifecycle hooks.
successCriteria: ref, onMounted, onUnmounted, and reactive are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some functions, but make sure to include ref, onMounted, onUnmounted, and reactive from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import ref, onMounted, onUnmounted, and reactive from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a default export component named App with a setup() function that returns an empty object.
steps.hint: Use the Vue composition API's setup() function to define the component's logic.
steps.seedCode:
import { ref, onMounted, onUnmounted } from 'vue'

// Create a default export component named App with a setup() function that returns an empty object
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named App is created with a setup() function that returns an empty object.
successCriteria: The component is exported as default, named App, has a setup() function, and returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the component is exported as default, named App, has a setup() function, and returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. Check that you've created a default export named App with a setup() function that returns an empty object.

steps.title: Initialize WebSocket connection state
steps.instruction: Inside the setup() function, use ref to create a reactive state variable named isConnected with an initial value of false.
steps.hint: Remember that ref() creates reactive state. You'll need to declare this variable before the return statement.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating reactive state
const isConnected = ref(false)
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a reactive isConnected state variable initialized to false.
successCriteria: isConnected is declared using ref() with initial value false inside setup()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using ref() to create the reactive state with initial value false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The isConnected state wasn't properly initialized. Check that you used ref() with false as the initial value.

steps.title: Initialize WebSocket message state
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a reactive messages array using ref to store received WebSocket messages.
steps.hint: Use the ref function to create a reactive reference initialized as an empty array.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating reactive state for messages
const messages = ref([])
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive messages array is created to store incoming WebSocket messages.
successCriteria: The messages state is declared using ref and initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using ref to create a reactive reference initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a reactive messages array using ref to store WebSocket messages.

steps.title: Initialize WebSocket instance reference
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a ref called 'socket' and initialize it to null.
steps.hint: Use the ref function you imported earlier to create a reactive reference for the WebSocket instance.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a reactive reference
const userInput = ref(null)
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive reference named 'socket' is created and initialized to null, ready to store the WebSocket connection instance.
successCriteria: The 'socket' ref is declared using ref(null) inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using ref(null) to initialize the socket reference.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a ref called 'socket' and set its initial value to null.

steps.title: Create WebSocket connection handler
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a function named connectWebSocket that will establish a WebSocket connection and set up event listeners.
steps.hint: Define the function using either function connectWebSocket() { ... } or const connectWebSocket = () => { ... }. The function body can be empty for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a connectWebSocket function defined in the setup function.
successCriteria: A function named connectWebSocket is defined inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a function named connectWebSocket inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The connectWebSocket function is not defined correctly. Please create a function named connectWebSocket inside the setup function.

steps.title: Set up component lifecycle hooks
steps.instruction: In the setup function, call onMounted to execute connectWebSocket when the component mounts, and call onUnmounted to execute disconnectWebSocket when the component unmounts.
steps.hint: Use the imported onMounted and onUnmounted functions. Pass your handler functions as arguments to these lifecycle hooks.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will automatically connect to the WebSocket when mounted and disconnect when unmounted.
successCriteria: onMounted is called with connectWebSocket, and onUnmounted is called with disconnectWebSocket.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some lifecycle hooks, but make sure both onMounted and onUnmounted are properly configured with their respective handler functions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The lifecycle hooks are not set up correctly. Remember to call onMounted with connectWebSocket and onUnmounted with disconnectWebSocket.

steps.title: Create the template structure
steps.instruction: Return a template from the setup function with a container div containing two sections: one for connection status and one for messages.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can return a template string from the setup function. Start with a div wrapper and add two sections inside.
steps.expectedOutcome: The setup function now returns a template property containing a div with two section elements.
successCriteria: The setup function returns an object with a template property containing a div wrapper and two section elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning an object with a template property containing the required structure.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure isn't quite right. Check that you're returning an object with a template property containing a div with two sections.

steps.title: Add connection controls and display state
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your setup function, add a template that displays the connection status, connect/disconnect buttons with click handlers, and a list of messages.
steps.hint: Use Vue's template syntax to bind data and methods. Display isConnected, call connectWebSocket and disconnectWebSocket on button clicks, and iterate through messages with v-for.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: template with data binding and event handlers return { isConnected: false, messages: [], connect() { /* connect logic */ }, disconnect() { /* disconnect logic */ }, template: `

Status: {{ isConnected ? 'Connected' : 'Disconnected' }}

  • {{ msg }}
` }
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a functional UI showing WebSocket connection status, buttons to connect/disconnect, and a list of received messages.
successCriteria: The return statement includes a template with: 1) Display of isConnected status, 2) Connect button with @click="connectWebSocket", 3) Disconnect button with @click="disconnectWebSocket", 4) List rendering of messages using v-for.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some UI elements, but make sure all required parts are present: connection status display, both buttons with correct click handlers, and message list rendering.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UI is missing or incorrect. Check that you've added the template with all required elements and proper Vue bindings.
